claim: `# Design: §11.3, §13.7, D-437.` above Constant, whose comment says 'A constant is never seeded, which is why it carries zero partials'
why: src/library.jl:324-325. spec.md:12287-12288 (§13.7) says 'A constant is never seeded, so it carries zero partials', and D-312 says the same. §11.3 (spec.md:8395-8399, 'No declaration constant could own that value') backs the docstring's 'A source set from outside is a root input'. D-437 backs the face `y` (src/library.jl:350 bare Pinned{V}).

claim: `# Design: §11.3, D-312, D-437.` above Source, whose comment says the output depends on neither state nor an input that follows the scalar, hence zero partials
why: src/library.jl:867-869 and :899-900: y_types is Pinned{V}, and y_state calls c.f(ForwardDiff.value(t)) with no state and no input. The D-312 annotation of 2026-10-06 (log.md) says a block whose output depends on neither its continuous state nor a walking input is never seeded, carries zero partials and pins. §11.3 backs the docstring's root-input sentence, and D-437 the face `y`. Probe P8c shows that f saw only Float64 time under a LinearizeDual build and linearize.

claim: code_map.md:759-849 names the helpers of the reset form (`reset_ports`, `signal`, `reset_guard`) but not `reset_handler`
why: src/library.jl:964 and :1875 each define a reset_handler method for their own component, Integrator and LimitedIntegrator. It is not a shared helper, and the discrete pair resets in s_update. code_map.md:8-10 has an entry name constructs, not list every method, and it names per-component handlers nowhere (step_handler, hit_upper_handler and the others are absent too). The helpers it names, reset_ports, signal and reset_guard (src/library.jl:450-453), are the shared ones.

claim: code_map.md lists the linear systems' helpers as `static_system`, `realize`, `coefficients_from_roots`, `transfer_coefficients` and the accessors, and omits the port helpers
why: src/library.jl:1041-1045 defines port_type, as_vector and as_port. code_map.md:8-10 makes no completeness claim. Its AbstractLinearSystem bullet covers port_type's role, 'over scalar or SVector ports by its matrix shapes', and the helpers it does name (static_system, realize, coefficients_from_roots, transfer_coefficients, held, realization, initial_state) exist at :1152, :1172, :1195 and :1346-1349.

claim: The TransferFunction and DiscreteTransferFunction docstrings (:1241, :1445) state the refusals of the root spelling as mixing the spellings, roots not closed under conjugation and more zeros than poles
why: src/library.jl:1195-1210 (transfer_coefficients) and :1172-1180. Probe P5d and P5h: mixing the spellings is an ArgumentError, continuous and discrete. P5b and P5i: an unpaired root is an ArgumentError. P5e: more zeros than poles is an ArgumentError. DiscreteTransferFunction at :1406-1408 defers to TransferFunction's refusals, and it calls the same helper (:1442). | The docstrings state these refusals correctly but do not say that a non-real gain is refused (src/library.jl:1203, probe P5f). A `zeros` or `gain` given without `poles` is also refused (P5g), which the signature lines imply by leaving `poles` without a default.

claim: D-183: the framework never inspects or mutates a workspace.
why: src/declare.jl:146-147 says the framework never reads or writes the workspace. `rg -i poison src` finds nothing. The workspace is only passed as the bundle's `ws` (src/build.jl:77, src/build.jl:1532). | src/conditions.jl:659-665 calls `ws_init` on a fresh allocation and checks `haskey` to label an undeclared condition field as `:workspace`. That reads the structure the allocator set up, not a live workspace's contents, which D-183's contract allows.

claim: D-280: the repository's test suite builds a `Dual` activation of every component.
why: src/build.jl:723-733 defines `ProbeDual` for this policy. test/test_library.jl builds Dual activations of the library components, for example test/test_library.jl:1314, test/test_library.jl:2171 and test/test_library.jl:3026 (`activations = (Float64, LinearizeDual[, ProbeDual])`), and test/test_build.jl:1818 does the same. | Spot-checked across the library testsets, not proved exhaustive for every component. Most tests list `LinearizeDual` rather than the entry's spelling `(Float64, ProbeDual)`. Both are `Dual` activations.

claim: D-283: if any unanchored discrete component exists, the deployment must declare `Δt_base`, and the refusal is constructive.
why: src/deployment.jl:253-258: `:derive` with any unanchored discrete component is refused as `DeploymentInvalid :unanchored` with the paths and the grid. Probe P4 message: '`ctl` is/are unanchored ... Declare the base tick period instead: `Δt_base = …` (§9.1)'. | Since D-443, leaving the keyword out takes `Δt_frame`, which counts as declaring it. Only derivation is refused.
